The current canonical authorization explicitly stops before issue comments, claims, forks, pushes, pull requests, terms, or payout steps.

Do not accept new bounty-platform terms, submit tax/identity/payment information, or configure payout rails without a separate Patrick-owned decision.
alternatives: Decline publication and keep the patch archived internally; no public GitHub action occurs.
Authorize only the issue claim comment, then hold again before fork/push/PR.
Wait for upstream baseline CI/install repairs before claiming, accepting the risk another contributor takes the bounty.
consequences: The GitHub account will make a public commercial contribution and may be associated with a bounty claim.
The advertised reward is USD 85 but payment is not guaranteed until maintainers accept/merge under their bounty process.
Fresh checks found the issue open with zero comments and no assignee before this hold was created.
The prepared targeted test suite passes 6 of 6 and new files pass ESLint, Prettier, and git diff checks.
Current upstream main independently has npm-ci lock/dependency problems, two pre-existing failing test suites, and unrelated TypeScript build errors; these are documented rather than hidden.
No spend, credentials, secrets, production access, payout setup, or customer data are required to publish the code contribution itself.
